brief.title: Falsify biomedical evidence-review pilot
brief.objective: Design a defensible Falsify pilot for evaluating whether biomedical research claims are supported by supplied papers. Choose abstract-first screening or full-text evidence extraction for a small manually curated corpus. Give a concrete evaluation and disagreement-resolution plan.
brief.context: Literature and software-methods research only. No patients, treatment decisions, doses or lab experiments. The product must distinguish unsupported, contradicted and unavailable evidence.

options: Abstract-first screening with explicit full-text escalation
Full-text extraction for every included paper
constraints: Only redistributable or user-provided licensed text
successCriteria: Trace each judgment to the relevant passage
Measure disagreement and evidence unavailability separately
knownFacts: No pilot annotations have been collected yet
assumptions: Full text will resolve more judgments than abstracts

documents.name: pilot-brief.md
documents.content: Proposal only: reviewers label claim, study population/model, measured outcome, supporting/contradictory passage and missing information. Abstract availability is not full-text availability. No accuracy percentage or completed validation is supplied.

rubric.notes: Separate evidential support from study quality and clinical relevance. Propose independent annotation, disagreement resolution, access handling and a small staged test. Do not invent sample-size justification or medical conclusions.
